title: Supreme Court Quashes 1990s Bengaluru Land Acquisition for Housing Society as a Fraud on Power
case_name: N. Arasappa v. State of Karnataka & Ors.
card_summary: The Supreme Court quashed a decades-old acquisition of around 59 acres at Nelakadirenahalli, Bengaluru, taken for a cooperative housing society. No approved housing scheme ever existed, and the society's own office bearers had told an inquiry committee that bribes were paid to push it through. Possession went back to the original owners; a 19-year delay and an earlier ruling did not bar the challenge.
card_tip: Delay and an adverse earlier ruling will not save a land acquisition once fraud or bribery in securing it is shown; such defects can be raised and undone years later.
verification_notes: Decision date (26 Oct 2026) and holding confirmed across LiveLaw's judgment report, ETV Bharat and Law Trend; figures on land area and compensation vary slightly between secondary reports, so the card states only the holding common to all three.
